subtopic: Reading 40 Introduction to Financial Statement Modeling
question_en: Which of the following would most likely lead to a company having high pricing power?
explanation_en: Pricing power is low when there are high levels of competition in the industry, when it is easy for customers to switch between products or have high bargaining power. Given a low threat of substitute products, the company is likely to have higher pricing power as there are fewer alternatives for the customers to choose from.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 40 Introduction to Financial Statement Modeling - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 40 Introduction to Financial Statement Modeling
question_en: An analyst is trying to compare the returns of two different firms, both operating in Europe. Why would the analyst most likely choose to use return on invested capital (ROIC) over return on equity (ROE)?
option_a: The two rms operate in dierent industries.
option_b: The two rms have diering capital structures.
option_c: The two rms operate in dierent countries.
explanation_en: ROIC is the return to both equity and debt as opposed to ROE, which only looks at the return to equity. ROIC can be helpful in analyzing firms with different capital structures. The industry or country that the firm operates in is less likely to make a difference to the choice of ROIC or ROE.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: Every six months a bond pays coupon interest equal to 3% of its par value. This bond is a:
explanation_en: The coupon rate on a bond is the percentage of its par value that it pays in interest each year. The coupon frequency states how often the bond will pay interest. A 6% semiannual coupon bond pays interest twice per year with each coupon equaling half of 6%, or 3%, of par value.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: Assuming bond yields are greater than zero, which of the following statements about zero- coupon bonds is least accurate?
option_a: A zero coupon bond may sell at a premium to par when interest rates decline.
option_b: All interest is earned at maturity.
option_c: The lower the price, the greater the return for a given maturity.
explanation_en: Zero coupon bonds always sell below their par value, or at a discount prior to maturity. The amount of the discount may change as interest rates change, but a zero coupon bond will always be priced less than par if it has a positive yield.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: An analyst observes a 5-year, 10% coupon bond with semiannual payments. The face value is £1,000. How much is each coupon payment?
explanation_en: The coupon rate is the percentage of par value paid annually. With semiannual coupons, half of the annual coupon rate is paid every six months. For a 5-year, 10% coupon bond with semiannual payments and a face value of £1,000, each coupon payment is half of 10% times £1,000, or £50.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: A covenant that requires the issuer not to let the insurance coverage lapse on assets pledged as collateral is an example of a(n):
explanation_en: Covenants are classified as negative or affirmative. Affirmative covenants specify administrative actions a bond issuer is required to take, such as maintaining insurance coverage on assets pledged as collateral. Negative covenants are restrictions on a bond issuer's actions, such as preventing an issuer from selling any assets that have been pledged as collateral or pledging them again as collateral for additional debt.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: Restrictions on asset sales and additional borrowings by a bond issuer are best characterized as:
explanation_en: Negative covenants are prohibitive in nature, such as restrictions on asset sales and additional borrowings. Affirmative or positive covenants are actions a borrower is required to take and are often administrative in nature, for example to comply with relevant laws and regulations or to insure and maintain assets.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following fixed income securities is classified as a money market security?
option_a: Newly issued security that will mature in one year.
option_b: Security issued 18 months ago that will mature in six months.
option_c: Security issued six months ago that will mature in one year.
explanation_en: Money market securities have original maturities of one year or less. Fixed income securities originally issued with maturities longer than one year are classified as capital market securities.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following contains the overall rights of the bondholders?
explanation_en: An indenture specifies the rights of bondholders and the obligations of the issuer. Covenants are specific provisions within the indenture. A rights offering is typically associated with an equity security.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: Features specified in a bond indenture least likely include the bond's:
explanation_en: Bond ratings are assigned by third-party credit rating agencies and may change during the life of a bond. Features that are specified in the indenture for a fixed income security include its issuer, maturity date, par value, coupon rate and frequency, and currency.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: A bond's indenture least likely specifies the:
option_b: covenants that apply to the issuer.
explanation_en: The identity of the lender (i.e., the bondholder) is not specified in a bond's indenture because a bond may be traded during its life. An indenture or trust deed is a legal contract that specifies a bond issuer's obligations and restrictions. The indenture may include covenants that require the issuer to take or refrain from taking certain actions and may specify the source of funds for repayment, such as a project to be funded or the taxing power of a government.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following bond covenants is considered negative?
explanation_en: Negative covenants set forth limitations and restrictions, whereas affirmative covenants primarily set forth administrative activities that the borrower promises to do.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 49 Fixed-Income Instrument Features - Answers.pdf
question_en: A bond is trading at a premium if its:
option_a: price is greater than its par value.
option_b: redemption value is greater than its face value.
option_c: yield is greater than its coupon rate.
explanation_en: If a bond's price is greater than its par value, the bond is trading at a premium. If a bond's yield is greater than its coupon rate, its price is less than par value and the bond is trading at a discount. Face value and redemption value both refer to par value.

The credit rating agencies suggest the company secure a third-party guarantee in order to have the security rated AAA. After completing the transfer of assets to the SPE and obtaining a letter of credit from a national bank, the company issues the AAA rated security. The securities are most likely:
explanation_en: Special purpose entities relate to asset-backed securities.

subtopic: Reading 50 Fixed-Income Cash Flows and Types
question_en: Treasury Inflation Protected Securities, which provide investors with protection against inflation by adjusting the par value and keeping the coupon rate fixed, are best described as:
explanation_en: Indexed bonds that adjust the principal value while keeping the coupon rate fixed are best described as capital-indexed bonds. Interest-indexed bonds adjust the coupon rate. Indexed-annuity bonds are fully amortizing with the payments adjusted.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 50 Fixed-Income Cash Flows and Types - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 50 Fixed-Income Cash Flows and Types
question_en: Which of the following statements about U.S. Treasury Inflation Protection Securities (TIPS) is most accurate?
option_a: The coupon rate is xed for the life of the issue.
option_b: Adjustments to principal values are made annually.
option_c: The ination-adjusted principal value cannot be less than par.
explanation_en: For U.S. Treasury TIPS, the coupon rate is set at a fixed rate determined via auction. The principal that serves as the basis of the coupon payment and the maturity value is adjusted semiannually. Because of the possibility of deflation, the adjusted principal value may be less than par. (However, at maturity, the Treasury redeems the bonds at the greater of the inflation-adjusted principal or the initial par value).

subtopic: Reading 50 Fixed-Income Cash Flows and Types
question_en: The indenture of a callable bond states that the bond may be called on the first business day of any month after the first call date. The call option embedded in this bond is a(n):
explanation_en: A bond with a Bermuda style embedded call option may be called on prespecified dates after the first call date. A European style embedded call option specifies a single date on which a bond may be called. With an American style embedded call option, a bond may be called any time after its first call date.

question_en: A bond has a par value of $5,000 and a coupon rate of 8.5% payable semi-annually. The bond is currently trading at 112.16. What is the dollar amount of the semi-annual coupon payment?
explanation_en: The dollar amount of the coupon payment is computed as follows: Coupon in $ = $5,000 × 0.085 / 2 = $212.50

subtopic: Reading 50 Fixed-Income Cash Flows and Types
question_en: Consider a floating rate issue that has a coupon rate that is reset on January 1 of each year. The coupon rate is defined as one-year London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) + 125 basis points and the coupons are paid semi-annually. If the one-year LIBOR is 6.5% on January 1, which of the following is the semi-annual coupon payment received by the holder of the issue in that year?
explanation_en: This value is computed as follows: Semi-annual coupon = (LIBOR + 125 basis points) / 2 = 3.875%

subtopic: Reading 50 Fixed-Income Cash Flows and Types
question_en: What effects will an increase in yield volatility have on the values of a putable bond and a callable bond?
option_a: One bond will increase in value and the other will decrease.
option_b: Both bonds will increase in value.
option_c: Both bonds will decrease in value.
explanation_en: A callable bond is made up of a straight bond and a written call option. An increase in volatility increases the value of the call option and decreases the value of the callable bond. On the other hand, a putable bond is made up of an option-free (or straight) bond and a long put option. An increase in volatility increases the value of the put option and therefore increases the value of the putable bond.
